setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "hub-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for hub-creator skill evals"

evals.name: filter-driven-tab-grid
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a hub eval_operations_hub with a Warehouse filter that scopes its single tab. The tab mounts eval_pick_velocity_grid (if that grid is not on the branch, first create a minimal version: flow-type embedded datasource, row shape { warehouse_name: string, pick_date: string, pick_count: number }). Selecting a warehouse in the hub filter must actually filter the grid's rows.
evals.expected_output: A hub whose filter → tab configParameters → grid inParams chain is wired consistently end to end — the grid (and its datasource) extended in the same change to declare the warehouse parameter, no dead wiring, correct moduleId, validated and upserted.
expectations: The hub has configurationTypeId 2, referenceName eval_operations_hub (snake_case, _hub suffix), and a non-empty description of at most 100 characters
The tab's configParameters binding for the warehouse filter uses a TypeScript-expression value of the form "$hub.filters.<id>.control.value"

Every id bound in the tab's configParameters is declared in the mounted grid's top-level inParams — since the grid did not originally declare a warehouse parameter, the agent EXTENDED the grid's inParams in the same change rather than leaving dead wiring where the hub passes a value the grid never receives

The chain continues into the grid's datasource: the new grid inParam is consumed downstream ($grid.inParams.<id> fed through datasourceConfig.configParameters, with the embedded datasource declaring the matching inParam and its flow code using it to filter rows)
The tab's configParameters covers EVERY inParam the grid declares — unused ones with value "" or null — and contains no extra entries for ids the grid does not declare
The tab's contentConfig moduleId is the GRID's package (the target's module), not the hub's
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate hub' run before 'dxs configuration upsert hub'
The transcript shows a wiring-contract audit before push (a component-wiring-check invocation, or an explicit cross-check of the tab's configParameters against the grid's inParams)

If the grid was extended, the grid edit used the corrected round-trip (dxs configuration get grid -O envelope.json, then jq .json extraction before editing) and the grid was re-validated and re-upserted

evals.name: hub-local-flow-no-dollar-flow
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a hub eval_engine_hub with an engine on/off toolbar toggle and a status label that must refresh both when the hub opens and after the toggle is clicked. Factor the shared refresh logic into one hub-local flow — the refresh logic needs to know which caller triggered it ('init' or 'toggle').
evals.expected_output: A hub whose shared local flow takes no inParams and never references $flow — the per-call value travels through a declared $hub.vars slot (or is inlined), the shared flow is invoked as $hub.<name>() from both call sites, and the hub validates before upsert.
expectations: No hub-local flow in the hub's flows[] declares inParams (inParams null or empty) — hub-local flows have no $flow global and cannot accept inParams
No hub-local flow body references $flow.inParams (or $flow at all) — flow bodies use $hub, $flows, $shell, $utils instead

The per-call trigger value reaches the shared flow via one of the two documented workarounds: each caller writes a declared $hub.vars.<id> before invoking the shared flow, or the logic is inlined at each call site with the value as a literal
The shared flow is invoked as $hub.<flow_referenceName>() from both the on_init path and the toggle click handler
Every $hub.vars.<id> written in flow code is declared in the hub's top-level vars[] array
Any backend work is invoked as a function via $flows.<Package>.<fn> — no direct action calls from hub code
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate hub' run before 'dxs configuration upsert hub', the referenceName ends in _hub, and the hub description is non-empty and at most 100 characters

evals.name: toolbar-button-and-selector-filter
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: eval_operations_hub should exist (if it does not, first create it per its earlier description with its warehouse filter and pick-velocity tab). Add (1) a Project filter backed by a projects selector — if no suitable selector exists on the branch, create a minimal eval_projects_dd first — and (2) an 'Options' toolbar button that opens eval_hub_options_form as a dialog (create a minimal form if missing) and refreshes the hub only when the form confirms.
evals.expected_output: A selector-backed filter whose configId/moduleId resolve to the selector's package with a complete dropdownConfig.configParameters mirror, plus a toolbar button whose click flow opens the dialog via $shell and refreshes only on confirmation — round-tripped, validated, upserted.
expectations: The new filter field's configId resolves to the projects selector and its moduleId is the SELECTOR's package (the target's module), not the hub's
Every configParameter the selector declares has an entry in the filter's dropdownConfig.configParameters — unused ones with value "" — with no missing and no extra entries (the mirror is complete)
The toolbar button's click flow opens the form via the generated $shell.<Package>.open<referenceName>Dialog(...) opener — not by invoking the form component any other way
The click flow calls $hub.refresh() only when the dialog result's confirmation flag (e.g. is_confirmed) is truthy — a cancelled dialog does not trigger a re-query

The button's click handler is wired via clickFlowConfig referencing a flow declared in the hub's flows[], and the new button id and filter id are unique within the hub (no collision with existing toolbar/tab/filter ids)

The hub modification used the corrected round-trip: 'dxs configuration get hub ... -O envelope.json' then extraction of the inner .json (jq .json or equivalent) before editing — the envelope was never piped directly back into upsert
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate hub' run before 'dxs configuration upsert hub'
If a selector or form was created as a prerequisite, it was created and upserted BEFORE the hub edit that references it

evals.name: role-gated-tab
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: add an Admin tab to eval_operations_hub (if the hub is not on the branch, first create it per its earlier description). The Admin tab mounts eval_warehouses_grid (create a minimal version if missing) and must be hidden from users who lack the admin permission.
evals.expected_output: A role-gated tab implemented the documented way: permission check in the on_init flow calling a function via $flows, deny path setting $hub.tabs.<id>.hidden = true, full configParameters contract on the new tab, correct moduleId, round-tripped and validated.
expectations: The access gate runs in the hub's on_init flow (onInitFlowConfig) — the permission check executes as the hub opens; the gate is not attempted via a nonexistent role/permission property on the tab config itself
On the deny path the flow hides the tab by setting $hub.tabs.<tab_id>.hidden = true (the documented mechanism for role-gated tabs)
The permission check invokes a function via $flows.<Package>.<fn> — no direct action call from hub code

The new Admin tab carries a full configParameters contract for the mounted grid: every grid inParam has an entry (unused ones with "" or null) and there are no extra entries for ids the grid does not declare
The Admin tab's contentConfig moduleId is the grid's package (the target's module), not the hub's

The hub edit used the corrected round-trip (dxs configuration get hub -O envelope.json, then jq .json extraction before editing), and 'dxs configuration validate hub' ran before 'dxs configuration upsert hub'
The new tab's id is unique within the hub (flow code addresses tabs by id; collisions silently overwrite)
